questions.stem: Which of the following actions will reduce risk to a laptop before traveling to a high risk area?
options: Examine the device for physical tampering
Implement more stringent baseline configurations
Purge or re-image the hard disk drive
Change access codes
questions.explanation: Wiping or re-imaging the laptop removes sensitive data so nothing is exposed if seized or compromised.
optionNotes: Inspection is for after return, not risk reduction before travel.
Hardening helps but data still present if seized.
Correct: removing sensitive data minimizes exposure.
Changing codes does not protect stored data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST network defense against unknown types of attacks or stealth attacks in progress?
options: Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS)
Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS)
Stateful firewalls
Network Behavior Analysis (NBA) tools
questions.explanation: NBA detects anomalies in traffic behavior, catching unknown and stealthy attacks that signatures miss.
optionNotes: IPS mostly signature-based; misses unknown attacks.
IDS signature engines miss novel attacks.
Stateful firewalls don't detect stealthy behaviour.
Correct: behaviour analysis detects anomalous/unknown activity.

questions.stem: Which of the following could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) against an authentication system?
options: Encryption of audit logs
No archiving of audit logs
Hashing of audit logs
Remote access audit logs
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said D] If logs are not archived they fill storage, and systems set to stop on full logs will deny authentication.
optionNotes: Encryption doesn't stop logging.
Correct: full logs can halt the system.
Hashing doesn't cause DoS.
Remote logs don't cause DoS.

questions.stem: When is a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) considered to be valid?
options: When it has been validated by the Business Continuity (BC) manager
When it has been validated by the board of directors
When it has been validated by all threat scenarios
When it has been validated by realistic exercises
questions.explanation: A BCP is validated only through realistic exercises/testing.
optionNotes: Manager approval isn't validation.
Board approval isn't validation.
Testing all scenarios is impossible.
Correct: realistic exercises validate the plan.

questions.stem: What would be the MOST cost effective solution for a Disaster Recovery (DR) site given that the organization's systems cannot be unavailable for more than 24 hours?
options: Warm site
Hot site
Mirror site
Cold site
questions.explanation: A warm site can be operational within roughly a day at much lower cost than a hot or mirror site.
optionNotes: Correct: warm site restorable within ~24h affordably.
Hot site works but costs more.
Mirror site is the most expensive.
Cold site takes too long.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY reason for implementing change management?
options: Certify and approve releases to the environment
Provide version rollbacks for system changes
Ensure that all applications are approved
Ensure accountability for changes to the environment
questions.explanation: Change management primarily ensures changes are controlled and accountable.
optionNotes: Release approval is a mechanism, not the purpose.
Rollback is a component.
Application approval is a narrower goal.
Correct: accountability and control for changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the FIRST step in the incident response process?
options: Determine the cause of the incident
Disconnect the system involved from the network
Isolate and contain the system involved
Investigate all symptoms to confirm the incident
questions.explanation: Incident response starts with detection/verification: confirm an incident actually exists before containment or root-cause work. Containment and disconnection (B, C) are tempting, but acting on an unconfirmed event can disrupt business for a false positive. ISC2 places detection and verification before containment.
optionNotes: Root cause analysis comes later, after containment.
Disconnecting is a containment action, done after confirmation.
Containment follows verification of the incident.
Right: first confirm a real incident exists (detection/verification).

questions.stem: What is the MOST important step during forensic analysis when trying to learn the purpose of an unknown application?
options: Disable all unnecessary services
Ensure chain of custody
Prepare another backup of the system
Isolate the system from the network
questions.explanation: Isolating the system stops the unknown application from communicating or spreading while it is studied. Chain of custody (B) matters for any evidence but does not help learn the application's purpose safely. Isolation lets analysts observe the program without it spreading, beaconing or exfiltrating data.
optionNotes: Disabling services could alter evidence and is not the key step.
Chain of custody matters for evidence but does not address safe study of the app.
Backups are useful but not the most important step here.
Right: isolation stops the unknown app from beaconing, spreading or exfiltrating.

questions.stem: What technique BEST describes antivirus software that detects viruses by watching anomalous behavior?
options: Signature
Inference
Induction
Heuristic
questions.explanation: Heuristic (behavior-based) detection flags anomalous behavior rather than known signatures. Signature engines match known code patterns and cannot catch new variants. Heuristic or behavior-based engines flag suspicious actions, which is what the stem describes.
optionNotes: Signature detection matches known patterns, not behavior.
Inference is not an AV detection technique.
Induction is not an AV detection technique.
Right: heuristic detection flags suspicious behavior.

questions.stem: In Disaster Recovery (DR) and business continuity training, which BEST describes a functional drill?
options: A full-scale simulation of an emergency and the subsequent response functions
A specific test by response teams of individual emergency response functions
A functional evacuation of personnel
An activation of the backup site
questions.explanation: A functional drill tests specific response functions by the teams, not a full-scale exercise. A full-scale simulation (A) is a full-scale exercise, and activating the backup site (D) is a parallel or full test. A functional drill exercises specific response functions by the relevant teams.
optionNotes: Full-scale simulation of all functions is a full-scale exercise.
Right: a functional drill tests particular response functions by teams.
Evacuation drill is just one narrow example.
Activating the backup site is a parallel/full test.

questions.stem: What should be the INITIAL response to Intrusion Detection System/Intrusion Prevention System (IDS/IPS) alerts?
options: Ensure that the Incident Response Plan is available and current.
Determine the traffic's initial source and block the appropriate port.
Disable or disconnect suspected target and source systems.
Verify the threat and determine the scope of the attack.
questions.explanation: Alerts must first be verified and scoped before taking response actions. IDS/IPS alerts include many false positives, so blocking ports or disconnecting systems (B, C) before analysis risks needless outages. First confirm the threat is real and size its scope.
optionNotes: Plan readiness should exist beforehand; not the response to an alert.
Blocking before verification may be wrong and disruptive.
Disconnecting before verification could disrupt operations needlessly.
Right: verify the alert is real and determine its scope first.

questions.stem: Which of the following Disaster Recovery (DR) sites is the MOST difficult to test?
options: Hot site
Cold site
Warm site
Mobile site
questions.explanation: A cold site lacks equipment, so it cannot be realistically tested until equipped. Hot and warm sites contain equipment that can be exercised. A cold site is an empty shell, so a realistic test means first procuring and installing everything.
optionNotes: Hot sites are fully equipped and readily tested.
Right: cold sites lack equipment, so meaningful testing is very hard.
Warm sites have some equipment and can be partially tested.
Mobile sites are equipped units and can be tested.

questions.stem: During an audit of system management, auditors find that the system administrator has not been trained. What actions need to be taken at once to ensure the integrity of systems?
options: A review of hiring policies and methods of verification of new employees
A review of all departmental procedures
A review of all training procedures to be undertaken
A review of all systems by an experienced administrator
questions.explanation: Immediate concern is system integrity, so an experienced admin should review all systems now. Hiring, procedure and training reviews (A–C) are valid follow-ups but slow. The urgent concern is whether the untrained admin already damaged system integrity, so an expert review comes at once.
optionNotes: Hiring policy review is a longer-term fix, not immediate.
Reviewing all procedures is broad and not urgent for integrity.
Training review is longer-term remediation.
Right: have an experienced admin check systems now for integrity issues.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the FIRST step to take when implementing a patch management program?
options: Perform automatic deployment of patches.
Monitor for vulnerabilities and threats.
Prioritize vulnerability remediation.
Create a system inventory.
questions.explanation: You must know what assets exist before monitoring, prioritizing, or deploying patches. Monitoring and prioritizing (B, C) only make sense once you know what exists. An accurate inventory tells you which vulnerabilities apply and where patches must go.
optionNotes: Deployment comes after inventory and prioritization.
Monitoring needs to know which assets matter.
Prioritization needs an inventory to work from.
Right: you cannot patch what you do not know you have.

questions.stem: What is the MOST important purpose of testing the Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)?
options: Evaluating the efficiency of the plan
Identifying the benchmark required for restoration
Validating the effectiveness of the plan
Determining the Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
questions.explanation: Testing validates that the plan actually works. Efficiency (A) is secondary, and the RTO (D) is set by the BIA. Testing exists to prove the plan actually works and to expose gaps.
optionNotes: Efficiency is secondary to whether the plan works.
Benchmarks are set in planning, not testing.
Right: testing validates the plan actually works.
RTO is set by the BIA, not determined by tests.

questions.stem: A system has been scanned for vulnerabilities and has been found to contain a number of communication ports that have been opened without authority. To which of the following might this system have been subjected?
options: Trojan horse
Denial of Service (DoS)
Spoofing
Man-in-the-Middle (MITM)
questions.explanation: Trojan horses often install backdoors that open listening ports for remote control. Unexpected, unauthorised open ports are therefore a classic sign of trojan infection.
optionNotes: Right: backdoor listeners open ports
DoS exhausts resources but does not open listening ports
Spoofing falsifies identity, it does not open ports
MITM intercepts traffic in transit, not on the host

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best practice for testing a Business Continuity Plan (BCP)?
options: Test before the IT Audit
Test when environment changes
Test after installation of security patches
Test after implementation of system patches
questions.explanation: A BCP must stay aligned with the business, so it should be tested when the environment changes significantly, in addition to scheduled testing.
optionNotes: Audit timing is not a valid test trigger
Right: changes may invalidate the plan
Security patches are too narrow a trigger
System patches are too narrow a trigger

questions.stem: A security professional has just completed their organization's Business Impact Analysis (BIA). Following Business Continuity Plan/Disaster Recovery Plan (BCP/DRP) best practices, what would be the professional's NEXT step?
options: Identify and select recovery strategies.
Present the findings to management for funding.
Select members for the organization's recovery teams.
Prepare a plan to test the organization's ability to recover its operations.
questions.explanation: The BIA establishes critical functions, MTD, RTO and RPO. The next BCP step is to identify and select recovery strategies that meet those targets.
optionNotes: Right: strategies follow BIA results
Funding requests follow strategy selection
Teams are formed during plan development
Testing comes after the plan exists

questions.stem: In the area of disaster planning and recovery, what strategy entails the presentation of information about the plan?
options: Communication
Planning
Recovery
Escalation
questions.explanation: Communication is the strategy for presenting plan information to stakeholders, staff and outside parties so everyone knows their role.
optionNotes: Right: presenting plan information
Planning develops the plan
Recovery restores operations
Escalation raises issues to higher authority

questions.stem: Which of the following is TRUE about Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) testing?
options: Operational networks are usually shut down during testing.
Testing should continue even if components of the test fail.
The company is fully prepared for a disaster if all tests pass.
Testing should not be done until the entire disaster plan can be tested.
questions.explanation: A DRP test should continue even if components fail, so the remaining steps are exercised and all gaps are found in one run.
optionNotes: Tests are designed to avoid disrupting production
Right: continue to uncover further gaps
Passing tests do not guarantee readiness
Partial and component tests are valuable and normal

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a fundamental objective in handling an incident?
options: To restore control of the affected systems
To confiscate the suspect's computers
To prosecute the attacker
To perform full backups of the system
questions.explanation: Incident handling aims to contain the incident and restore control and normal operation of affected systems; prosecution and seizure are secondary.
optionNotes: Containment and restoring control of systems is the core goal
Seizing equipment is a possible forensic step, not the objective
Prosecution is an optional management decision
Backups support recovery but are not the objective

questions.stem: At a MINIMUM, a formal review of any Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) should be conducted
options: monthly.
quarterly.
annually.
bi-annually.
questions.explanation: DR plans should be formally reviewed at least annually and after significant changes.
optionNotes: Monthly formal review is good practice for some items but not the stated minimum
Quarterly exceeds the minimum requirement
Annual review (plus after major change) is the accepted minimum
Every two years leaves the plan stale

questions.stem: Which of the following is a network intrusion detection technique?
options: Statistical anomaly
Perimeter intrusion
Port scanning
Network spoofing
questions.explanation: Statistical anomaly (behaviour-based) detection compares traffic to a baseline and is an IDS technique.
optionNotes: Baseline-deviation detection is a classic IDS method
Perimeter intrusion is a physical concept, not a detection technique
Port scanning is reconnaissance the IDS detects
Spoofing is an attack the IDS detects

questions.stem: Which one of these risk factors would be the LEAST important consideration in choosing a building site for a new computer facility?
options: Vulnerability to crime
Adjacent buildings and businesses
Proximity to an airline flight path
Vulnerability to natural disasters
questions.explanation: Crime, neighbours and natural disasters are major siting factors; proximity to a flight path is a low-probability concern.
optionNotes: Crime exposure is a major siting factor for asset protection
Neighbours bring fire, hazmat and access risks
A flight path is a remote, low-likelihood risk
Natural disasters are a primary siting concern

questions.stem: Contingency plan exercises are intended to do which of the following?
options: Train personnel in roles and responsibilities
Validate service level agreements
Train maintenance personnel
Validate operation metrics
questions.explanation: Exercises train personnel in their roles and responsibilities and validate plan workability.
optionNotes: Exercises build familiarity with roles and responsibilities
SLAs are validated through monitoring, not plan exercises
Maintenance staff training is too narrow
Operational metrics are not the exercise goal

questions.stem: Which of the following is ensured when hashing files during chain of custody handling?
options: Availability
Accountability
Integrity
Non-repudiation
questions.explanation: Hashes prove evidence has not changed, ensuring integrity.
optionNotes: Hashing doesn't keep evidence accessible
Accountability comes from custody signatures/logs
Matching hashes prove the evidence is unchanged
A hash lacks a private-key signature, so no non-repudiation

questions.stem: How can a forensic specialist exclude from examination a large percentage of operating system files residing on a copy of the target system?
options: Take another backup of the media in question then delete all irrelevant operating system files.
Create a comparison database of cryptographic hashes of the files from a system with the same operating system and patch level.
Generate a message digest (MD) or secure hash on the drive image to detect tampering of the media being examined.
Discard harmless files for the operating system, and known installed programs.
questions.explanation: Hashing known-good OS files (e.g., NSRL-style databases) lets the examiner exclude matching files without altering evidence.
optionNotes: Deleting files from evidence copies taints the examination
Known-file hash sets let matching OS files be excluded safely
Image hashes verify integrity, not exclude files
Arbitrarily discarding files is unsound forensics

questions.stem: Who must approve modifications to an organization's production infrastructure configuration?
options: Technical management
Change control board
System operations
System users
questions.explanation: Production configuration changes are approved by the change control board.
optionNotes: Technical managers advise but don't own approval
The CCB formally approves production changes
Operations implement approved changes
Users request but don't approve

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A new employee is given a laptop computer with full administrator access. This employee does not have a personal computer at home and has a child that uses the computer to send and receive e-mail, search the web, and use instant messaging. The organization's Information Technology (IT) department discovers that a peer-to-peer program has been installed on the computer using the employee's access. Which of the following methods is the MOST effective way of removing the Peer-to-Peer (P2P) program from the computer?
options: Run software uninstall
Re-image the computer
Find and remove all installation files
Delete all cookies stored in the web browser cache
questions.explanation: Re-imaging returns the system to a known-good state, removing the P2P program and any hidden components.
optionNotes: Uninstall may leave files/registry and hidden payloads
Re-imaging guarantees a known-good baseline
Manual removal is error-prone and incomplete
Cookies are unrelated to the installed program

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A security practitioner detects client-based attacks on the organization's network. A plan will be necessary to address these concerns. In the plan, what is the BEST approach to mitigate future internal client-based attacks?
options: Block all client side web exploits at the perimeter.
Remove all non-essential client-side web services from the network.
Screen for harmful exploits of client-side services before implementation.
Harden the client image before deployment.
questions.explanation: Internal client-based attacks are best prevented by reducing the attack surface of the clients themselves through a hardened standard image before deployment. Perimeter blocking does not stop internal vectors.
optionNotes: Perimeter controls miss internal and encrypted client attacks.
Impractical and still leaves client software exposed.
Screening helps but is narrower than hardening the whole build.
Correct: hardening the client image reduces exploitable surface on every endpoint.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A security practitioner detects client-based attacks on the organization's network. A plan will be necessary to address these concerns. What is the BEST reason for the organization to pursue a plan to mitigate client-based attacks?
options: Client privilege administration is inherently weaker than server privilege administration.
Client hardening and management is easier on clients than on servers.
Client-based attacks are more common and easier to exploit than server and network based attacks.
Client-based attacks have higher financial impact.
questions.explanation: Clients are the most frequently targeted and easiest-to-exploit entry point through browsing, email and user interaction. That prevalence and ease of exploitation is the best reason to prioritize a plan.
optionNotes: Not necessarily true and not the main driver.
False; clients are harder to manage at scale.
Correct: client-based attacks are the most common and easiest avenue.
Impact varies; not inherently higher.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. During the investigation of a security incident, it is determined that an unauthorized individual accessed a system which hosts a database containing financial information. Aside from the potential records which may have been viewed, which of the following should be the PRIMARY concern regarding the database information?
options: Unauthorized database changes
Integrity of security logs
Availability of the database
Confidentiality of the incident
questions.explanation: Beyond the viewing of records, an intruder with database access may have altered financial data. Unauthorized changes to financial records undermine their trustworthiness and are the primary concern.
optionNotes: Correct: integrity of financial data is the key concern after unauthorized access.
Log integrity matters for the investigation, not the database information itself.
No indication availability was affected.
Concerns the incident handling, not the database information.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A new employee is given a laptop computer with full administrator access. This employee does not have a personal computer at home and has a child that uses the computer to send and receive e-mail, search the web, and use instant messaging. The organization's Information Technology (IT) department discovers that a peer-to-peer program has been installed on the computer using the employee's access. Which of the following solutions would have MOST likely detected the use of peer-to-peer programs when the computer was connected to the office network?
options: Anti-virus software
Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)
Anti-spyware software
Integrity checking software
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer traffic has distinctive network signatures that a network IPS can detect when the laptop joins the office network. Endpoint malware tools focus on malicious code, not legitimate-but-forbidden applications.
optionNotes: Antivirus targets malicious code, not P2P usage.
Correct: an IPS inspects traffic and can detect P2P protocols.
Spyware tools do not detect P2P traffic.
Integrity checking detects file changes, not network use.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A security practitioner detects client-based attacks on the organization's network. A plan will be necessary to address these concerns. What MUST the plan include in order to reduce client-side exploitation?
options: Approved web browsers
Network firewall procedures
Proxy configuration
Employee education
questions.explanation: Client-side exploits commonly rely on user actions like opening attachments or visiting malicious sites. Employee education is required to reduce such exploitation.
optionNotes: Helps but does not address user behaviour.
Network procedures do not target client behaviour.
Technical detail, not a must-have.
Correct: user awareness reduces client-side exploitation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to determine if a particular system is able to identify malicious software without executing it?
options: Testing with a Botnet
Testing with an EICAR file
Executing a binary shellcode
Run multiple antivirus programs
questions.explanation: The EICAR test file is a harmless standard string that antimalware should detect statically, so it tests detection without executing real malware.
optionNotes: A botnet is live malware and needs execution/infrastructure.
Right: EICAR is a harmless standard file AV should detect statically.
Running shellcode means executing code, the opposite of what's asked.
Running multiple AV products doesn't test this system's detection.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes Recovery Time Objective (RTO)?
options: Time of data validation after disaster
Time of data restoration from backup after disaster
Time of application resumption after disaster
Time of application verification after disaster
questions.explanation: RTO is the maximum tolerable time to resume the business application/function after a disruption.
optionNotes: Data validation is part of recovery, not the RTO itself.
Restoring data is a step; RPO concerns data loss.
Right: RTO is the target time to resume the application/function.
Verification is a step inside recovery.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization experiencing a negative financial impact is forced to reduce budgets and the number of Information Technology (IT) operations staff performing basic logical access security administration functions. Security processes have been tightly integrated into normal IT operations and are not separate and distinct roles. Which of the following will MOST likely allow the organization to keep risk at an acceptable level?
options: Increasing the amount of audits performed by third parties
Removing privileged accounts from operational staff
Assigning privileged functions to appropriate staff
Separating the security function into distinct roles
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said D] With reduced staff and budget, creating separate security roles is unrealistic. Assigning privileged functions only to appropriate staff applies least privilege and keeps risk acceptable.
optionNotes: More third-party audits costs money during cuts and only detects issues.
Removing privileges entirely stops admin work from getting done.
Right: least privilege with the existing staff fits the budget.
Separate roles need staff the organization no longer has.

questions.stem: Host-Based Intrusion Protection (HIPS) systems are often deployed in monitoring or learning mode during their initial implementation. What is the objective of starting in this mode?
options: Automatically create exceptions for specific actions or files
Determine which files are unsafe to access and blacklist them
Automatically whitelist actions or files known to the system
Build a baseline of normal or safe system events for review
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said A] Learning mode records normal system events to build a baseline that administrators review before enforcement. This reduces false positives once blocking is turned on.
optionNotes: Exceptions should come from reviewed baselines, not be created automatically
Learning mode doesn't identify unsafe files
Automatic whitelisting without review is not the objective
Builds a reviewed baseline of normal events

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST reason to review audit logs periodically?
options: Verify they are operating properly
Monitor employee productivity
Identify anomalies in use patterns
Meet compliance regulations
questions.explanation: The purpose of regular log review is detection: spotting anomalous or suspicious usage that may indicate misuse or attack. Compliance may require it, but detection is the security reason.
optionNotes: Checking logging works is a side benefit, not the main reason
Productivity monitoring is not a security objective of log review
Finding anomalies enables detection of incidents and misuse
Compliance is a driver but not the BEST security reason

questions.stem: What should happen when an emergency change to a system must be performed?
options: The change must be given priority at the next meeting of the change control board.
Testing and approvals must be performed quickly.
The change must be performed immediately and then submitted to the change board.
The change is performed and a notation is made in the system log.
questions.explanation: Emergency changes are implemented right away to restore or protect operations, then documented and submitted to the change board for after-the-fact review and approval. Change management still applies, just retroactively.
optionNotes: Waiting for the next board meeting defeats the emergency
Rushed testing/approval still delays and is not the defined emergency path
Implement now, then submit to the CAB for retroactive review
A log note alone bypasses change management review

questions.stem: The PRIMARY security concern for handheld devices is the
options: strength of the encryption algorithm.
spread of malware during synchronization.
ability to bypass the authentication mechanism.
strength of the Personal Identification Number (PIN).
questions.explanation: Handheld devices sync with corporate systems, giving malware a path into the network. That propagation risk is the primary concern in this classic question.
optionNotes: Algorithm strength is rarely the weak point
Synchronization can spread malware between device and network
Authentication bypass is a concern but less primary
PIN strength is a narrower concern

questions.stem: While investigating a malicious event, only six days of audit logs from the last month were available. What policy should be updated to address this problem?
options: Retention
Reporting
Recovery
Remediation
questions.explanation: The retention policy sets how long logs are kept. Only six days being available shows that policy needs updating.
optionNotes: Retention governs how long logs are kept
Reporting concerns communicating results
Recovery concerns restoring systems
Remediation concerns fixing issues

questions.stem: Retaining system logs for six months or longer can be valuable for what activities?
options: Disaster recovery and business continuity
Forensics and incident response
Identity and authorization management
Physical and logical access control
questions.explanation: Breaches are often found long after they happen, so long log retention lets investigators reconstruct events for forensics and incident response.
optionNotes: DR/BC rely on backups, not logs
Long-retained logs support forensics and IR
IAM doesn't depend on old logs
Access control is preventive, not log-based

questions.stem: Which of the following activities BEST identifies operational problems, security misconfigurations, and malicious attacks?
options: Policy documentation review
Authentication validation
Periodic log reviews
Interface testing
questions.explanation: Regular log review reveals operational errors, misconfigurations and attack traces across systems.
optionNotes: Reviewing policy documents finds no live misconfigurations or attacks
Authentication validation covers one control only
Log reviews surface operational faults, misconfigurations and attacks
Interface testing checks functionality, not ongoing operations

questions.stem: What type of test assesses a Disaster Recovery (DR) plan using realistic disaster scenarios while maintaining minimal impact to business operations?
options: Parallel
Walkthrough
Simulation
Tabletop
questions.explanation: A simulation exercises realistic scenarios without activating recovery sites or disrupting operations.
optionNotes: Parallel tests activate recovery systems, more effort and impact
Walkthroughs only review the plan, no realistic scenario play
Simulation enacts realistic scenarios without disrupting operations
Tabletop is discussion-based, less realistic than simulation

questions.stem: What operations role is responsible for protecting the enterprise from corrupt or contaminated media?
options: Information security practitioner
Information librarian
Computer operator
Network administrator
questions.explanation: The media librarian controls media handling and checks media to prevent corrupt or contaminated media from entering the environment.
optionNotes: Practitioner is too general a role
Media librarian controls and checks media entering use
Operators run systems but do not own media control
Network admins manage networks, not media

questions.stem: How does a Host Based Intrusion Detection System (HIDS) identify a potential attack?
options: Examines log messages or other indications on the system.
Monitors alarms sent to the system administrator
Matches traffic patterns to virus signature files
Examines the Access Control List (ACL)
questions.explanation: A HIDS analyses host data such as logs, system files and events to detect attacks.
optionNotes: HIDS inspects host logs, files and events
Alarms are HIDS output, not its detection method
Matching virus signatures in traffic describes AV/NIDS
ACL review is not how HIDS detects attacks

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important consideration when developing a Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)?
options: The dynamic reconfiguration of systems
The cost of downtime
A recovery strategy for all business processes
A containment strategy
questions.explanation: A DRP must provide recovery strategies covering the business processes identified by the BIA.
optionNotes: Dynamic reconfiguration is a technical detail
Downtime cost informs the BIA but is not the DRP focus
Recovery strategies for business processes are the DRP core
Containment belongs to incident response

questions.stem: After acquiring the latest security updates, what must be done before deploying to production systems?
options: Use tools to detect missing system patches
Install the patches on a test system
Subscribe to notifications for vulnerabilities
Assess the severity of the situation
questions.explanation: Patches must be tested on non-production systems to confirm they do not break functionality before deployment.
optionNotes: Detecting missing patches precedes acquisition
Testing patches on non-production prevents outages
Vulnerability notifications precede acquiring patches
Severity assessment comes before acquiring, not deployment

questions.stem: What is the GREATEST challenge of an agent-based patch management solution?
options: Time to gather vulnerability information about the computers in the program
Requires that software be installed, running, and managed on all participating computers
The significant amount of network bandwidth while scanning computers
The consistency of distributing patches to each participating computer
questions.explanation: Agent-based solutions require agents installed, running and maintained on every managed host.
optionNotes: Agents gather data efficiently; not the challenge
Installing and managing agents everywhere is the burden
Agents reduce scanning bandwidth
Agents improve distribution consistency

questions.stem: To protect auditable information, which of the following MUST be configured to only allow read access?
options: Logging configurations
Transaction log files
User account configurations
Access control lists (ACL)
questions.explanation: Log files must be read-only to preserve their integrity as audit evidence.
optionNotes: Logging configs must be changeable by admins
Log files must be read-only to preserve audit integrity
Account configs need administrative changes
ACLs must be modifiable to manage access

questions.stem: In configuration management, what baseline configuration information MUST be maintained for each computer system?
options: Operating system and version, patch level, applications running, and versions.
List of system changes, test reports, and change approvals
Last vulnerability assessment report and initial risk assessment report
Date of last update, test report, and accreditation certificate
questions.explanation: Baselines record OS and version, patch level and installed applications with versions.
optionNotes: OS, patch level, applications and versions define the baseline
Change records are change management, not baseline
Assessment reports are not baseline configuration
Accreditation data is not baseline configuration

questions.stem: Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) training material should be
options: consistent so that all audiences receive the same training.
stored in a fire proof safe to ensure availability when needed.
only delivered in paper format.
presented in a professional looking manner.
questions.explanation: Consistent training material ensures everyone gets the same accurate understanding of the plan.
optionNotes: Consistency ensures everyone receives the same accurate content
Safe storage concerns plan copies, not training
Paper-only delivery is needlessly restrictive
Presentation polish does not drive effectiveness

questions.stem: Network-based logging has which advantage over host-based logging when reviewing malicious activity about a victim machine?
options: Addresses and protocols of network-based logs are analyzed.
Host-based system logging has files stored in multiple locations.
Properly handled network-based logs may be more reliable and valid.
Network-based systems cannot capture users logging into the console.
questions.explanation: Network logs are captured off the victim host, so an attacker who compromises the host cannot easily alter them. Handled with proper chain of custody they are more trustworthy evidence.
optionNotes: Analysis of addresses is possible but not the key advantage.
Describes a host-log drawback, not a network advantage.
Right: independent of the compromised host, hence more reliable.
A limitation of network logging, not an advantage.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the BEST configuration management practice?
options: After installing a new system, the configuration files are copied to a separate back-up system and hashed to detect tampering.
After installing a new system, the configuration files are copied to an air-gapped system and hashed to detect tampering.
The firewall rules are backed up to an air-gapped system.
A baseline configuration is created and maintained for all relevant systems.
questions.explanation: Configuration management centres on establishing and maintaining baselines for systems so deviations are controlled. Backups of configuration files are useful but are narrow measures.
optionNotes: Backup and hashing is one control, not the overall practice.
Same narrow backup step, just air-gapped.
Covers only firewall rules.
Right: baseline configuration is the core of CM.

questions.stem: A network scan found 50% of the systems with one or more critical vulnerabilities. Which of the following represents the BEST action?
options: Assess vulnerability risk and program effectiveness.
Assess vulnerability risk and business impact.
Disconnect all systems with critical vulnerabilities.
Disconnect systems with the most number of vulnerabilities.
questions.explanation: Before acting, management needs to know the actual risk and what the affected systems mean to the business. Mass disconnection without analysis could cause more harm than the vulnerabilities.
optionNotes: Program effectiveness is secondary to immediate risk decisions.
Right: risk and business impact drive prioritisation.
Disconnecting half the estate could cripple operations.
Vulnerability count is not the same as risk.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN reason for using configuration management?
options: To provide centralized administration
To reduce the number of changes
To reduce errors during upgrades
To provide consistency in security controls
questions.explanation: Configuration management keeps systems in known, approved states so controls are applied consistently. Fewer errors or centralisation are side benefits.
optionNotes: Centralisation is a means, not the purpose.
CM controls changes, not reduces them.
Fewer upgrade errors is a side benefit.
Right: consistent, known configurations.

questions.stem: Which of the following disaster recovery test plans will be MOST effective while providing minimal risk?
options: Read-through
Parallel
Full interruption
Simulation
questions.explanation: A parallel test activates the recovery site and processes for real while production keeps running. It validates recovery far better than paper tests without the risk of a full interruption.
optionNotes: Read-through tests only documents.
Right: real recovery test with production unaffected.
Most effective but highest risk.
Simulation does not actually process at the recovery site.

questions.stem: Reciprocal backup site agreements are considered to be
options: a better alternative than the use of warm sites.
difficult to test for complex systems.
easy to implement for similar types of organizations.
easy to test and implement for complex systems.
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said C] Reciprocal (mutual assistance) agreements look cheap, but OSG lists their drawbacks: they are hard to enforce and hard to test, and the partner may lack spare capacity. They are especially impractical to test, and often cannot support, complex systems. The dump's claim that they are easy to implement goes against this guidance.
optionNotes: Wrong: warm sites are generally more reliable than an unenforceable MAA.
Correct: complex systems cannot realistically be tested on another organization's live production setup.
Wrong: confidentiality, capacity and enforcement problems make MAAs hard to implement even between similar organizations.
Wrong: complex systems are the hardest case to test and implement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important element of change management documentation?
options: List of components involved
Number of changes being made
Business case justification
A stakeholder communication
questions.explanation: Every change has to be justified by business need. The business case is what lets the change advisory board weigh the benefit against the risk and approve or reject the change.
optionNotes: The component list is useful detail but secondary.
The number of changes is not meaningful on its own.
Correct: the business justification drives the approval decision.
Communication matters but comes after the decision.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a common risk with network configuration management?
options: Patches on the network are difficult to keep current.
It is the responsibility of the systems administrator.
User ID and passwords are never set to expire.
Network diagrams are not up to date.
questions.explanation: Configuration management relies on accurate documentation. Outdated network diagrams are a common risk that undermines change management, troubleshooting and incident response.
optionNotes: Patching is patch management, not configuration management.
Assigning responsibility to an admin is not a risk.
Password expiry is an identity management issue.
Correct: stale diagrams are a typical configuration management weakness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason to use manual patch installation instead of automated patch management?
options: The cost required to install patches will be reduced.
The time during which systems will remain vulnerable to an exploit will be decreased.
The likelihood of system or application incompatibilities will be decreased.
The ability to cover large geographic areas is increased.
questions.explanation: Installing manually allows testing and careful staging, which lowers the risk of incompatibilities breaking systems. Automation wins on cost, speed and scale.
optionNotes: Manual installation costs more.
Manual installation leaves systems vulnerable for longer.
Correct: controlled installation reduces incompatibilities.
Automation covers large areas better.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of controls should allow an investigation if an attack is not blocked by preventive controls or detected by monitoring?
options: Logging and audit trail controls to enable forensic analysis
Security incident response lessons learned procedures
Security event alert triage done by analysts using a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system
Transactional controls focused on fraud prevention
questions.explanation: If prevention and monitoring both miss an attack, investigators still need logs and audit trails to reconstruct what happened. That is what makes forensic analysis possible.
optionNotes: Correct: logs and audit trails enable after-the-fact investigation.
Lessons learned follow an investigation; they do not enable it.
SIEM triage is part of the monitoring that failed.
Fraud controls are preventive and specific to transactions.

questions.stem: How does an organization verify that an information system's current hardware and software match the standard system configuration?
options: By reviewing the configuration after the system goes into production
By running vulnerability scanning tools on all devices in the environment
By comparing the actual configuration of the system against the baseline
By verifying all the approved security patches are implemented
questions.explanation: Configuration verification means comparing the system's actual state against its approved baseline. Any deviation from the baseline is a configuration drift that must be resolved.
optionNotes: Timing of review is irrelevant; it still needs a baseline to compare to.
Vulnerability scans find weaknesses, not baseline conformance.
Correct: baseline comparison verifies configuration.
Patches are only one part of the configuration.

questions.stem: The restoration priorities of a Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) are based on which of the following documents?
options: Service Level Agreement (SLA)
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)
Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
Crisis management plan
questions.explanation: The BIA identifies critical business functions, their impacts and the MTD/RTO values, which set the order in which systems are recovered in the DRP.
optionNotes: SLAs define service levels with providers, not recovery priority.
The BCP consumes BIA output but is not the source of priorities.
Correct: BIA determines criticality and recovery priorities.
The crisis management plan addresses communications and command.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason for employing physical security personnel at entry points in facilities where card access is in operation?
options: To verify that only employees have access to the facility.
To identify present hazards requiring remediation.
To monitor staff movement throughout the facility.
To provide a safe environment for employees.
questions.explanation: Under ISC2 doctrine, life safety is the overriding purpose of physical security, and guards provide judgement and response that card readers cannot, protecting people at the facility.
optionNotes: Card readers already verify credentials; guards add more than this.
Hazard identification is a facilities role, not the primary guard purpose.
Monitoring movement is a secondary function.
Correct: guards primarily support a safe environment for people.

questions.stem: Which of the following MUST be in place to recognize a system attack?
options: Stateful firewall
Distributed antivirus
Log analysis
Passive honeypot
questions.explanation: Recognizing an attack requires reviewing recorded events; log analysis is the essential detection activity, whatever tools generate the data.
optionNotes: Firewalls block traffic but do not recognize attacks alone.
Antivirus detects malware only.
Correct: log analysis is required to recognize attacks.
Honeypots are optional.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of a change management policy?
options: To assure management that changes to the Information Technology (IT) infrastructure are necessary
To identify the changes that may be made to the Information Technology (IT) infrastructure
To verify that changes to the Information Technology (IT) infrastructure are approved
To determine the necessity of implementing modifications to the Information Technology (IT) infrastructure
questions.explanation: Change management ensures every change is reviewed and approved before implementation, preventing unauthorized changes.
optionNotes: Assuring necessity is part of review, not the main purpose.
Identifying changes is a step, not the purpose.
Correct: verify changes are approved.
Determining necessity is part of review.

questions.stem: Unused space in a disk cluster is important in media analysis because it may contain which of the following?
options: Residual data that has not been overwritten
Hidden viruses and Trojan horses
Information about the File Allocation table (FAT)
Information about patches and upgrades to the system
questions.explanation: Slack space in a cluster can still hold remnants of previously written files, a key source of recoverable evidence.
optionNotes: Correct: residual data remains in slack.
Malware may hide but is not the main reason.
FAT information is stored elsewhere.
Patch info is not in slack.

questions.stem: A company receives an email threat informing of an Imminent Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack targeting its web application, unless ransom is paid. Which of the following techniques BEST addresses that threat?
options: Deploying load balancers to distribute inbound traffic across multiple data centers
Set Up Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) to filter out malicious traffic
Implementing reverse web-proxies to validate each new inbound connection
Coordinate with and utilize capabilities within Internet Service Provider (ISP)
questions.explanation: A volumetric DDoS can overwhelm the company's own links before any on-premises control acts; the ISP can filter upstream.
optionNotes: Load balancers still saturate under large floods.
WAFs sit behind the saturated link.
Reverse proxies also sit downstream.
Correct: upstream ISP mitigation is most effective.

questions.stem: A Security Operations Center (SOC) receives an incident response notification on a server with an active intruder who has planted a backdoor. Initial notifications are sent and communications are established. What MUST be considered or evaluated before performing the next step?
options: Notifying law enforcement is crucial before hashing the contents of the server hard drive
Identifying who executed the incident is more important than how the incident happened
Removing the server from the network may prevent catching the intruder
Copying the contents of the hard drive to another storage device may damage the evidence
questions.explanation: Before containment by disconnecting, the team should weigh that removal may alert the intruder and lose the chance to observe or catch them.
optionNotes: Notification does not have to precede hashing.
How it happened matters more for recovery.
Correct: containment trade-off must be evaluated.
Proper imaging with write blockers does not damage evidence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important part of an awareness and training plan to prepare employees for emergency situations?
options: Having emergency contacts established for the general employee population to get information
Conducting business continuity and disaster recovery training for those who have a direct role in the recovery
Designing business continuity and disaster recovery training programs for different audiences
Publishing a corporate business continuity and disaster recovery plan on the corporate website
questions.explanation: Training must be tailored to each audience so everyone knows their role in an emergency.
optionNotes: Contacts help but are not training.
Training only recovery staff omits others.
Correct: audience-specific programs.
Publishing the plan is not training.

questions.stem: A company seizes a mobile device suspected of being used in committing fraud. What would be the BEST method used by a forensic examiner to isolate the powered-on device from the network and preserve the evidence?
options: Put the device in airplane mode
Suspend the account with the telecommunication provider
Remove the SIM card
Turn the device off
questions.explanation: Airplane mode cuts network connections while keeping the device powered and its volatile data intact.
optionNotes: Correct: isolates without losing state.
Suspending the account may not stop Wi-Fi.
SIM removal may alter evidence.
Powering off loses volatile data and may trigger encryption.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to reduce the impact of an externally sourced flood attack?
options: Have the service provider block the source address.
Have the source service provider block the address.
Block the source address at the firewall.
Block all inbound traffic until the flood ends.
questions.explanation: Blocking at the upstream provider stops flood traffic before it saturates the company's link.
optionNotes: Correct: the provider blocks upstream.
The source's provider is not under your control.
The firewall is behind the saturated link.
Blocking all traffic is self-DoS.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN reason for testing a Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)?
options: To ensure Information Technology (IT) staff knows and performs roles assigned to each of them
To validate backup sites' effectiveness
To find out what does not work and fix it
To create a high level DRP awareness among Information Technology (IT) staff
questions.explanation: Testing finds weaknesses in the plan so they can be corrected before a real disaster.
optionNotes: Role knowledge is a by-product.
Validating sites is one part.
Correct: find and fix what fails.
Awareness is secondary.

questions.stem: Why is planning in Disaster Recovery (DR) an interactive process?
options: It details off-site storage plans
It identifies omissions in the plan
It defines the objectives of the plan
It forms part of the awareness process
questions.explanation: DR planning is iterative: each review and test cycle turns up gaps and omissions that feed back into the plan.
optionNotes: Off-site storage is plan content, not why the process iterates
Correct: each review/test cycle exposes omissions, which feed back into the plan
Objectives are set once at the start; this doesn't make planning iterative
Awareness is a by-product, not the reason for iteration

questions.stem: What can happen when an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is installed inside a firewall-protected internal network?
options: The IDS can detect failed administrator logon attempts from servers.
The IDS can increase the number of packets to analyze.
The firewall can increase the number of packets to analyze.
The firewall can detect failed administrator login attempts from servers
questions.explanation: An internal IDS sees internal host traffic such as failed admin logons that a perimeter firewall never examines.
optionNotes: Correct: an internal IDS sees host-to-host events such as failed admin logons
Analyzing more packets is a load effect, not a capability
The firewall's packet load does not change because of an IDS
Internal server logons never cross the perimeter firewall

questions.stem: Which of the following would BEST support effective testing of patch compatibility when patches are applied to an organization's systems?
options: Standardized configurations for devices
Standardized patch testing equipment
Automated system patching
Management support for patching
questions.explanation: Standardized configurations make test results representative of production, so patch compatibility testing is reliable.
optionNotes: Correct: uniform baselines mean test results represent production
Test hardware helps only if it matches production configurations
Automation deploys patches; it does not test compatibility
Management support is needed but does not directly enable effective testing

questions.stem: Which of the following would an attacker BEST be able to accomplish through the use of Remote Access Tools (RAT)?
options: Reduce the probability of identification
Detect further compromise of the target
Destabilize the operation of the host
Maintain and expand control
questions.explanation: RATs give persistent remote control, so attackers can keep and expand their foothold.
optionNotes: RATs are often detected; stealth is not their main purpose
Detecting compromise is the defender's goal
Destabilizing the host is a DoS objective
Correct: a RAT gives persistent remote control for pivoting

questions.stem: A user has infected a computer with malware by connecting a Universal Serial Bus (USB) storage device. Which of the following is MOST effective to mitigate future infections?
options: Develop a written organizational policy prohibiting unauthorized USB devices
Train users on the dangers of transferring data in USB devices
Implement centralized technical control of USB port connections
Encrypt removable USB devices containing data at rest
questions.explanation: A centralized technical control that blocks USB ports enforces the restriction directly, unlike policy or training.
optionNotes: Policy alone is an administrative control and is easily ignored
Training helps but doesn't enforce anything
Correct: central technical blocking directly prevents recurrence
Encryption protects confidentiality, not malware entry

questions.stem: A minimal implementation of endpoint security includes which of the following?
options: Trusted platforms
Host-based firewalls
Token-based authentication
Wireless Access Points (AP)
questions.explanation: A host-based firewall is a baseline endpoint control expected on every endpoint.
optionNotes: Desirable but not minimal
Correct: basic endpoint protection
Authentication control, not endpoint minimum
Network infrastructure, not endpoint

questions.stem: Which of the following management process allows ONLY those services required for users to accomplish their tasks, change default user passwords, and set servers to retrieve antivirus updates?
options: Configuration
Identity
Compliance
Patch
questions.explanation: Disabling unneeded services, changing defaults and setting update sources are hardening tasks under configuration management.
optionNotes: Correct: secure baseline configuration
Manages identities
Checks conformity, does not set config
Applies vendor fixes only

questions.stem: What does electronic vaulting accomplish?
options: It protects critical files.
It ensures the fault tolerance of Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) systems
It stripes all database records
It automates the Disaster Recovery Process (DRP)
questions.explanation: Electronic vaulting transfers backups of critical files to an offsite location, protecting them.
optionNotes: Correct: bulk offsite transfer of backups protects critical files
RAID fault tolerance comes from parity/mirroring, not vaulting
Striping is a RAID technique, not a vaulting function
Vaulting supplies recovery data but does not automate the DR process

questions.stem: After following the processes defined within the change management plan, a super user has upgraded a device within an Information system. What step would be taken to ensure that the upgrade did NOT affect the network security posture?
options: Conduct an Assessment and Authorization (A&A)
Conduct a security impact analysis
Review the results of the most recent vulnerability scan
Conduct a gap analysis with the baseline configuration
questions.explanation: A security impact analysis evaluates whether a change affected the security posture.
optionNotes: Full A&A is excessive for one change
An old scan predates the change
Correct: SIA examines the change's security effect
Baseline gap analysis shows drift, not posture impact

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST efficient mechanism to account for all staff during a speedy nonemergency evacuation from a large security facility?
options: Large mantrap where groups of individuals leaving are identified using facial recognition technology
Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) sensors worn by each employee scanned by sensors at each exit door
Emergency exits with push bars with coordinates at each exit checking off the individual against a predefined list
Card-activated turnstile where individuals are validated upon exit
questions.explanation: RFID tags read automatically at exits account for staff quickly.
optionNotes: A mantrap with facial recognition creates a bottleneck
Correct: passive RFID reads count people without slowing exit
Manual checklists at each exit are slow and error-prone
Turnstiles slow a mass exit

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY objective of the post-incident phase of the incident response process in the security operations center (SOC)?
options: Improve the IR process.
Communicate the IR details to the stakeholders.
Validate the integrity of the IR.
Finalize the IR.
questions.explanation: The post-incident (lessons learned) phase exists to improve the incident response process: the team reviews what happened, what worked and what did not, and feeds those findings back into plans, controls and training. Communicating with stakeholders and closing out the case happen too, but they serve that improvement goal rather than replace it.
optionNotes: Correct: lessons learned improve the IR process
Stakeholder communication occurs but is secondary
Integrity validation is part of evidence handling, not the phase goal
Closing the ticket is administrative, not the objective

questions.stem: Who should formulate conclusions from a particular digital forensics analysis and submit a report of the results?
options: The information security professional's supervisor
Legal counsel for the information security professional's employer
The information security professional who conducted the analysis
A peer reviewer of the information security professional
questions.explanation: The examiner who performed the analysis draws and reports conclusions, since they can testify to them. Conclusions must come from the person with first-hand knowledge of the methods and findings.
optionNotes: The supervisor did not perform the analysis.
Counsel advises on law, not technical conclusions.
The examiner who did the work can support and testify to the conclusions.
Peer review validates, it doesn't author the conclusions.

questions.stem: What is the MOST important criterion that needs to be adhered to during the data collection process of an active investigation?
options: Capturing an image of the system
Maintaining the chain of custody
Complying with the organization's security policy
Outlining all actions taken during the investigation
questions.explanation: Chain of custody preserves evidence admissibility. Without it, the evidence may be inadmissible however well it was collected.
optionNotes: Imaging is a step, not the governing criterion.
Chain of custody preserves admissibility.
Policy compliance is secondary to evidentiary integrity.
Notes support custody but custody is the key criterion.

questions.stem: Which of the following technologies would provide the BEST alternative to anti-malware software?
options: Host-based Intrusion Detection Systems (HIDS)
Application whitelisting
Host-based firewalls
Application sandboxing
questions.explanation: Whitelisting only permits approved code, blocking unknown malware. It is a default-deny approach that doesn't depend on signatures.
optionNotes: HIDS detects rather than prevents.
Whitelisting allows only approved code, blocking unknown malware.
Host firewalls filter network traffic, not malicious code.
Sandboxing contains but still runs unknown code.

questions.stem: A scan report returned multiple vulnerabilities affecting several production servers that are mission critical. Attempts to apply the patches in the development environment have caused the servers to crash. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Upgrade the software affected by the vulnerability.
Inform management of possible risks.
Mitigate the risks with compensating controls.
Remove the affected software from the servers.
questions.explanation: When patches can't be applied without breaking mission-critical servers, the risk still has to be reduced while a fix is worked out. Compensating controls such as segmentation, IPS rules or tighter access lower the exposure without the outage. Simply informing management doesn't reduce the risk on its own.
optionNotes: Upgrading carries the same instability risk as the failed patches and may not be feasible quickly.
Management should be informed, but by itself this leaves the vulnerabilities open.
Right: compensating controls reduce the risk while keeping critical servers running.
Removing software from mission-critical servers would disrupt the business.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important consideration that must be taken into account when deploying an enterprise patching solution that includes mobile devices?
options: Service provider(s) utilized by the organization
Whether it will impact personal use
Number of mobile users in the organization
Feasibility of downloads due to available bandwidth
questions.explanation: Mobile devices often connect over limited or metered cellular links, so pushing large patches may not be possible or may be costly. Bandwidth determines whether patches can actually reach devices.
optionNotes: The carrier matters less than whether patches can be delivered at all.
Personal-use impact is a secondary user-experience concern.
User count affects scale but the infrastructure can be sized for it.
Right: limited mobile bandwidth decides whether patches can be downloaded.

questions.stem: What is maintained by using write blocking devices when forensic evidence is examined?
options: Inventory
Integrity
Confidentiality
Availability
questions.explanation: Write blockers prevent any changes to the evidence media while it is examined. That preserves its integrity and keeps it admissible.
optionNotes: Inventory isn't what write blockers protect.
Right: they preserve evidence integrity.
Write blockers don't prevent disclosure.
They aren't about availability.

questions.stem: An organization has implemented a new backup process which protects confidential data by encrypting the information stored on backup tapes. Which of the following is a MAJOR data confidentiality concern after the implementation of this new backup process?
options: Tape backup rotation
Pre-existing backup tapes
Tape backup compression
Backup tape storage location
questions.explanation: The new process only encrypts tapes from now on, so tapes created earlier still hold confidential data in clear text. Those pre-existing tapes remain a confidentiality exposure.
optionNotes: Rotation affects availability and retention, not confidentiality of the new encrypted tapes.
Right: older unencrypted tapes still expose data.
Compression doesn't affect confidentiality.
Location matters less once tapes are encrypted; the older tapes are the gap.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the order in which a digital forensic process is usually conducted?
options: Ascertain legal authority, agree upon examination strategy, conduct examination, and report results
Ascertain legal authority, conduct investigation, report results, and agree upon examination strategy
Agree upon examination strategy, ascertain legal authority, conduct examination, and report results
Agree upon examination strategy, ascertain legal authority, report results, and conduct examination
questions.explanation: Investigators must first confirm they have legal authority, then plan the examination strategy, carry out the examination, and finally report. Starting without authority risks inadmissible evidence.
optionNotes: Right: authority, strategy, examination, report.
Reporting before agreeing on strategy is out of order.
Strategy before legal authority is out of order.
Reporting before examining is illogical.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important rule for digital investigations?
options: Ensure event logs are rotated.
Ensure original data is never modified.
Ensure individual privacy is protected.
Ensure systems are powered on.
questions.explanation: The core rule of digital forensics is to preserve the original evidence unaltered, working on verified copies. Any modification can make the evidence inadmissible.
optionNotes: Log rotation can destroy evidence.
Right: never modify original data.
Privacy matters but is secondary to evidence integrity here.
Powering systems on can alter evidence.

questions.stem: If virus infection is suspected, which of the following is the FIRST step for the user to take?
options: Unplug the computer from the network.
Save the opened files and shutdown the computer.
Report the incident to service desk.
Update the antivirus to the latest version.
questions.explanation: Users are not responders; their first action is to report the suspected infection to the service desk so the incident response process can begin. Isolating, shutting down or patching are response decisions that could destroy evidence or bypass the IR process.
optionNotes: Containment decision belongs to the response team
Shutdown destroys volatile evidence
Correct: report via proper channel
Does not address the incident

questions.stem: In fault-tolerant systems, what do rollback capabilities permit?
options: Restoring the system to a previous functional state
Identifying the error that caused the problem
Allowing the system to run in a reduced manner
Isolating the error that caused the problem
questions.explanation: Rollback returns a system to a previously known good state after a failure. It lets operations resume from a consistent checkpoint rather than diagnosing or isolating the fault.
optionNotes: Correct: returns the system to a checkpointed good state
Root-cause diagnosis is a separate troubleshooting step
Running degraded is fail-soft, not rollback
Fault isolation is containment, not rollback

questions.stem: What term is commonly used to describe hardware and software assets that are stored in a configuration management database (CMDB)?
options: Configuration element
Asset register
Ledger item
Configuration item
questions.explanation: Items tracked in a CMDB are configuration items (CIs). Each CI is recorded with its attributes and relationships so changes can be controlled.
optionNotes: Not ITIL/CMDB vocabulary
An asset register is a financial inventory, not CMDB records
Ledger items are accounting terms
Correct: ITIL calls CMDB records configuration items (CIs)

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST comprehensive Business Continuity (BC) test?
options: Full functional drill
Full tdue top
Full simulation
Full interruption
questions.explanation: A full interruption test actually shuts down primary operations, making it the most comprehensive (and risky) test. Tabletop, simulation and functional drills all leave production running, so they are less complete.
optionNotes: Tests systems but keeps production running
Discussion-based only
Walks through a scenario without stopping operations
Correct: actually fails over from primary operations

questions.stem: Which of the following processes has the PRIMARY purpose of identifying outdated software versions, missing patches, and lapsed system updates?
options: Penetration testing
Vulnerability management
Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
Life cycle management
questions.explanation: Vulnerability management identifies missing patches and outdated software. Penetration testing exploits weaknesses, while SDLC and lifecycle management are broader processes.
optionNotes: Exploits flaws and is periodic, not systematic
Correct: scans for missing patches and old versions
Development process
Broad asset lifecycle

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes botnets?
options: Computer systems on the Internet that are set up to trap people who attempt to penetrate other computer system
Set of related programs that protects the resources of a private network from other networks
Small network inserted in a neutral zone between an organization's private network and the outside public network
Groups of computers that are used to launch destructive attacks
questions.explanation: Botnets are groups of compromised computers used to launch attacks. Honeypots, firewalls and DMZs are defensive constructs, not botnets.
optionNotes: Describes a honeypot
Describes a firewall
Describes a DMZ
Correct: compromised hosts under a C2 controller

questions.stem: What is the MOST common cause of Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) compromise?
options: Port scan
Brute force attack
Remote exploit
Social engineering
questions.explanation: Exposed RDP is most commonly compromised by credential brute forcing. Attackers scan for exposed port 3389 and then try credential stuffing or guessing against weak passwords.
optionNotes: Reconnaissance, not the compromise itself
Correct: password guessing against exposed RDP
Exploits such as BlueKeep exist but are less common
Plausible but not the dominant cause

questions.stem: When conducting a forensic criminal investigation on a computer hard drive, what should be done PRIOR to analysis?
options: Create a backup copy of all the important files on the drive.
Power off the computer and wait for assistance.
Create a forensic image of the hard drive.
Install forensic analysis software.
questions.explanation: Analysis must be performed on a verified forensic image to preserve the original evidence. A bit-for-bit image with hash verification preserves the original; copying files misses slack space and changes metadata.
optionNotes: Logical copy misses slack space and changes metadata
Pulling the plug may be wrong and analysis still needs an image
Correct: preserves the original evidence
Installing software alters the evidence

questions.stem: What is the MOST common component of a vulnerability management framework?
options: Risk analysis
Patch management
Threat analysis
Backup management
questions.explanation: Patch management is the most common component of vulnerability management. Most vulnerability programs focus on finding missing patches and deploying them, which makes patching the most common component.
optionNotes: Supports prioritization
Correct: the most common fix activity
Feeds prioritization
Recovery, not vulnerability handling

questions.stem: The security team is notified that a device on the network is infected with malware. Which of the following is MOST effective in enabling the device to be quickly located and remediated?
options: Data loss protection (DLP)
Intrusion detection
Vulnerability scanner
Information Technology Asset Management (ITAM)
questions.explanation: Asset management records ownership and location of devices, enabling quick location and remediation. Without an accurate inventory, alerts cannot be tied to a physical device, an owner or a location.
optionNotes: Prevents exfiltration but does not locate the device
Alerts on activity but does not give location
Finds weaknesses, not ownership
Correct: inventory gives location and owner

questions.stem: An organization discovers that its secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) server has been accessed by an unauthorized person to download an unreleased game. A recent security audit found weaknesses in some of the organization's general information technology (IT) controls, specifically pertaining to software change control and security patch management, but not in other control areas. Which of the following is the MOST probable attack vector used in the security breach?
options: Buffer overflow
Weak password due to lack of complexity rules
Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
questions.explanation: Weak patch management leaves known flaws such as buffer overflows exploitable on the server. Audit findings point to unpatched software, which suggests a technical exploit rather than password guessing.
optionNotes: Correct
Password controls not flagged
Availability, not data theft
Client-side web attack

questions.stem: What is the MOST effective response to a hacker who has already gained access to a network and will attempt to pivot to other resources?
options: Reset all passwords.
Shut down the network.
Warn users of a breach.
Segment the network.
questions.explanation: Segmentation contains the attacker and prevents lateral movement. Resetting passwords may not remove an existing foothold, and shutting the whole network down is disproportionate.
optionNotes: Does not remove an existing foothold
Disproportionate disruption
Does not contain the attacker
Correct: limits lateral movement

questions.stem: Which is the MOST critical aspect of computer-generated evidence?
options: Objectivity
Integrity
Timeliness
Relevancy
questions.explanation: Digital evidence is easily altered without leaving a trace. For it to be admissible and trusted, it must be shown to be unchanged, using hashes and chain of custody. Integrity is therefore the most critical aspect.
optionNotes: Objectivity matters for analysis but does not establish that the evidence is authentic
Right: you must prove the evidence was not altered
Prompt collection helps but is not the defining requirement
Every type of evidence must be relevant; this is not specific to computer evidence

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN benefit of off-site storage?
options: Cost effectiveness
Backup simplicity
Fast recovery
Data availability
questions.explanation: Off-site storage keeps backup copies away from the primary site. If that site is destroyed, the data is still available for recovery, which is its main purpose.
optionNotes: Off-site storage adds transport and storage costs
Backup procedures become more complex, not simpler
Retrieving media from off site can actually slow recovery
Right: data stays available if the primary site is lost

questions.stem: Which of the following is the key requirement for test results when implementing forensic procedures?
options: The test results must be cost-effective.
The test result must be authorized.
The test results must be quantifiable.
The test results must be reproducible.
questions.explanation: Forensic results must be repeatable: another examiner using the same method should reach the same results. This is what makes findings defensible in court.
optionNotes: Cost does not make a forensic result valid
Authorization is needed to collect evidence, but it is not a property of the test results
